rationale: Different classes are valid: invalid pairs (5,3), (3,6), (4,3), and (5,4) put 3,4,5,6 together. Valid (1,4), (8,1), and (8,4) require three distinct classes.
Valid (4,4) requires same-class agreement. Valid pairs connect 1,2,3,5,6,7,8; invalid (4,8), (4,5), and (4,3) separate token 4.
Invalid (5,5) requires different-class agreement. Invalid (6,8) and (3,8) group 3,6,8; valid (5,6), (8,5), (1,3), and (8,1) separate 1,5 from that group. Valid (2,4) separates 2 and 4.

Invalid (4,4) requires different-class agreement. Invalid (4,1), (5,4), (6,5), and (5,1) group 1,4,5,6; invalid (7,3) groups 7,3. All valid pairs cross the assigned classes, including (8,2) and (8,7).
Valid (4,4), (3,3), and (2,2) require same-class agreement. Invalid (7,2), (2,5), and (5,7) require three distinct classes; the remaining invalid pairs also cross the assigned classes.

Invalid (6,6) requires different-class agreement. Invalid (4,7) and (5,7) group 4,5,7; invalid (1,8) groups 1,8. Valid (5,6) and (1,6) place 6 in a third class; valid (3,5), (2,3), and (2,6) are reproduced.
Valid (4,4) and (5,5) require same-class agreement. Valid pairs connect 3,5,6,7,8 and separately connect 2,4. Invalid (2,6), (4,8), and (8,1) separate their assigned classes.

Valid (1,1) requires same-class agreement, and valid (8,2) groups 8,2. Invalid (7,2), (7,6), and (2,6) require three distinct classes. Token 5 differs from 2 and 7, while token 3 differs from 5 and 6; every invalid demonstration crosses classes.
